keyFindings: The ~300 set is a count of LISTINGS (merchant-product pairs), not distinct products. Effective product diversity is 13-16 distinct products per query, each appearing up to 30 times from different merchants.
Duplication ratio: 18.8x to 23.1x. The catalog returns the same ~15 products from every merchant that stocks them.
Every presence figure should be read against the smaller number (~15 distinct products), not 300.

CONTROLLED COMPARISON FOUND: The PRL Motorsports High Volume Intake System for 2023 Honda Civic Type R FL5 appears 30 times in the Catalog from different merchants. Subimods stocks this product but Subimods' own listing is absent (present=false, rank=null). This is the controlled comparison DIRECTIVE-7 §6 was reaching for: same product, multiple merchants present, one merchant absent — with the product held constant.
For BC Racing BR Series coilovers: MAP, Springrates, and JDMuscle all stock it and all are present. No absent merchant for this part.
For brake pads and downpipes: scanned stores that stock these parts are present. No absent merchant.
implications: The Subimods case is not store-wide absence — it is per-product absence. Subimods' OEM Subaru parts ARE in the Catalog; their aftermarket performance parts are NOT. This is the partial syndication observation that DIRECTIVE-13 §1 (H7) is built on.

The controlled comparison (PRL intake: 30 merchants present, Subimods absent) sharpens the invisibility claim: it is not that the product is invisible, but that one merchant's listing of it is invisible.

The ~300 boundary is the relevance threshold for listings. With only ~15 distinct products, the catalog exhausts its supply of relevant products quickly and fills the remaining slots with duplicate listings from other merchants.
